column15: Core range is standard unpeated Speyside malt (majority goes into Label 5/Cutty Sark blends). A distinct Peated/Smoky expression exists, see rule.tsv.
Whole range uses local Orkney peat (higher heather content) at a moderate level, matching the brief's own medium examples (Talisker/Bowmore).

Luxury 21yo+ blend based on Strathisla (Speyside); no peat/smoke mentioned anywhere in the scotchwhisky.com profile I read in full. Treated as none on absence of any smoke/peat descriptor, not an explicit unpeated statement, hence low confidence.

Official site (ei-sake.jp) describes the Akashi single malt's taste as '...medium, light, slightly peaty'; the Akashi blended whisky is described as smooth/dry with no peat mention. Legal distillery name is White Oak (Eigashima Shuzo); no separate White Oak catalogue entry in this batch so Akashi is modelled as the distillery-level row. defaultTypeName left empty: range spans single malt and blended.

Standard unpeated Highland malt, un-chill filtered, natural colour. NOTE FOR REVIEWER: Wikipedia (fetched today) names the current owner as CVH Spirits Limited, successor to Distell/Burn Stewart Distillers -- flag if another batch's Bunnahabhain/Tobermory rows (same ownership family) assume plain 'Distell'.
Core Madeira/Sherrywood/Portwood expressions are unpeated. A distinct Peated expression (and the Dragon range's 'Celt') exists, see rule.tsv.
Triple-distilled Lowland malt; universally unpeated house style, samples (Three Wood, American/Blood/Dark Oak) are all cask-finish variants of the same unpeated spirit.

Irish whiskey range (Founder's Reserve style blend + Harvest editions) by Walsh Whiskey; ownership not independently re-verified this session. Irish whiskey is 'almost always' unpeated per the general Whisky article; defaultTypeName left empty since the range spans blend and single-malt-style expressions.
Wheated bourbon distilled in Loretto, Kentucky. American whiskey production does not use peat-smoked malt.

No web presence found this session: Wikipedia search (multiple phrasings), Bing search, and domain probes (fauconnier.fr is unrelated, other guesses did not resolve) all came up empty. Samples 'O'Brian Fauconnier'/'Fauconnier Hunting Lodge'/'Fauconnier Highland's Friends' suggest an obscure own-label blend, but country/type/peat could not be confirmed -- left unknown rather than guessed. Flag for human review.

Small-batch New Zealand single malt distillery in the Waikato region (near the Bombay Hills). Official site's homepage and 'Our Whisky' page state no peat/smoke information for any expression (Ringbearer, Core Range, Exploration Series, Single Casks) -- left unknown rather than guessed.

Closed 1902 (as Glen Grant #2) then 1965-2002, demolished 2010; historically a standard Speyside blending malt for Chivas Regal, no peat mentioned anywhere in its Wikipedia article. IMPORTANT FOR REVIEWER: 3 of the 5 catalogue sample names read 'Caperdonich Peated' -- I could not find any citation confirming this expression exists or its intensity (scotchwhisky.com has no Caperdonich page at the URL I tried, no Wikipedia mention of a peated Caperdonich). Deliberately wrote NO rule for it rather than invent one; flag for human review, possibly an independent-bottler cask exception.

Catalogue brand string 'Kentucky' bundles apparently unrelated products: Fordman, Wiseman, Benchmark No 8, Kentucky Walker (x2). Benchmark is confirmed real (Sazerac Company's Benchmark Old No. 8 bourbon, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sazerac_Company), but Wiseman/Fordman/Kentucky Walker could not be confirmed and may be generic import-market bourbon-style products, possibly not even genuine American whiskey. peatProfile=none reflects the American-whiskey category norm (peat-kilning is a Scotch-specific technique per the Whisky article), not a verified single house style. Flag for human review -- this brand may need splitting per-product in a later pass.

Standard blended Scotch; owner (Inver House Distillers/International Beverage) is from general trade knowledge, NOT confirmed by a citation opened this session (the Inver House Distillers Wikipedia article I fetched does not actually mention Catto's by name) -- flag for reviewer to verify ownership independently. peatProfile=none is a category default for an ordinary blend (grain-whisky-led per the Blended whiskey article), not a Catto's-specific citation.

Could not identify the producer. Investigated two candidates: Eigashima Shuzo's White Oak distillery (maker of Akashi) and Matsui Shuzo's Kurayoshi/Matsui brand family -- Matsui's own official site (matsuiwhisky.com) lists Kurayoshi/Matsui/Tottori/San-in/Daisen but no product called 'Kura', so that link is unconfirmed. 'White Oak' in the sample name 'Kura White Oak' may simply denote the American-white-oak cask species rather than a brand reference. Left fully unknown rather than guess; flag for human review.

Independent bottler/whisky broker, named after the Argyll mountain pass; no dedicated citation found this session (Wikipedia and Bing searches returned nothing on point), general trade-knowledge identification only, hence low confidence even on category. Samples name two REAL distilleries (Benrinnes, Bruichladdich -- rows emitted below, per authority file) plus 'Strathenry' and 'Finglassie', which do NOT appear in the Wikipedia Scottish-distilleries authority list (259 rows) -- treated as invented/undisclosed single-cask names per the brief's undisclosed-label rule, no distillery row created for them and no guess made at the true source.
Family-owned (Kulsveen family) Bardstown, Kentucky producer of bourbon and rye (traded as Kentucky Bourbon Distillers 1984-2012). defaultTypeName left empty: range spans both bourbon and rye.

Irish whiskey range (Vintage Grain, Fortitude, Legacy Reserve). No Wikipedia article found this session confirming producer/ownership; general knowledge points to P. & H. Egan Ltd (Tullamore) but this is unverified this session, left owner empty. Category default applied for peat (Irish whiskey almost always unpeated).

Tasmanian (Burnie) distillery founded 1997 by Betta Milk dairy farmers. No peat/smoke mentioned in its Wikipedia profile -- treated as unpeated on absence of a statement rather than an explicit claim, hence low confidence.

Ezra Brooks-family line bottled by Lux Row Distillers (see lux-row row in this file). Samples span both rye ('Rye Full Proof') and bourbon ('7 Bourbon Barrel Strength'), so defaultTypeName left empty. American whiskey category default applied for peat.

No web presence found (Wikipedia search empty). All 3 samples are just 'Charles House' with no other descriptor. Treated as an ordinary own-label blend per the brief's long-tail rule; country left unknown rather than guessed.

Louisville, Kentucky bourbon distillery known for port-cask finishing (its whole signature, not a separate 'Port Cask' sub-brand -- the two samples are both just the core product). Ownership (Bacardi Limited, acquired 2015) is from general knowledge; a dedicated Wikipedia fetch attempted this session 404'd on the title tried, so that specific fact is NOT independently re-verified -- only the general Whisky article backs the peat=none category claim.
Major Johnnie Walker blend component; standard unpeated Speyside malt, uncontroversial and well documented.

No web presence under this exact spelling: Wikipedia search returned zero hits and its own fuzzy-match suggestion was unrelated ('glentaisie'), not 'Glenlossie'. Possibly a misspelling of Glenlossie (Speyside, Diageo -- per the local authority file) or a genuinely obscure/fictional own-brand. Deliberately left unlinked to Glenlossie to avoid an incorrect alias -- flag for human review.

Non-distiller-producer bourbon aged/finished at sea; ownership (Pernod Ricard, via Castle Brands/Jefferson's Bourbon Co. since 2019) from general knowledge, not re-verified with a fresh citation this session -- only the general Whisky article backs the peat=none category claim.

Bardstown, Kentucky distillery opened 2018; producer of the Ezra Brooks family (see old-ezra row), Rebecca Creek, and its own Lux Row-branded bourbons (Four Grain, Double Barrel/PX Sherry Finish). Ownership chain from general knowledge, not freshly verified this session -- only the general Whisky article backs the peat=none category claim.

Historic Powers brand's flagship pot-still expression, distilled at Midleton. 'midleton' is a well-known Irish distillery slug that another batch will very likely emit (home of Jameson/Redbreast/Midleton Very Rare) -- not created in this file to avoid a low-value duplicate. Category default applied for peat.

Irish whiskey blend named for the 1850s NYC gang / present-day NYC bar. No distillery/ownership citation found this session. Category default applied (Irish whiskey almost always unpeated, Connemara being the well-known exception).

Presumed independent-bottler/single-cask range, named for the traditional worm-tub condenser (a term associated with a handful of old-style Scottish distilleries). No dedicated citation found this session. No distillery is named in its own samples ('Wormtub', 'Wormtub Single Cask - Batch 6'), so no additional distillery row was emitted for it.

Part of Jim Beam's small-batch bourbon collection (alongside Knob Creek/Basil Hayden/Booker's), distilled at Jim Beam's Clermont/Boston, KY site. 'jim-beam' is an extremely well-known distillery slug another batch will almost certainly emit -- not created here.
No web presence found (single product, no distinguishing sample). Irish-themed own-label blend pattern, category default applied per the brief's long-tail rule.
No web presence found (single product). Named for Dublin's Fitzwilliam Square; treated as an Irish-themed own-label blend, category default applied.
Historic Owensboro, Kentucky bourbon brand revived by Green River Distilling Co.; sample 'Green River Wheated' confirms a wheated mash bill. Ownership not freshly verified this session.

Historic Kentucky brand revived as 'James E. Pepper 1776', distilled at the rebuilt Pepper distillery (Lexington/Georgetown, KY). Range spans both bourbon and rye under the 1776 label, so defaultTypeName left empty. Ownership not freshly verified this session.

Closed Lowland distillery (authority file lists no current owner following its 2004 closure/2008 fire). Standard unpeated Lowland style applied by region default, not independently re-confirmed with a dedicated Littlemill peat citation this session.
No web presence found (single product). Named for Ireland's southernmost point; own-label Irish whiskey pattern, category default applied.

One of the oldest continuously produced American whiskey brands (since 1810), produced at Jim Beam's distillery. 'jim-beam' is a well-known distillery slug another batch will almost certainly emit -- not created here.

Single product 'Ley Seca' (Spanish for 'dry law' / Prohibition). No whiskey/whisky brand by this name found on Wikipedia; 'Ley Seca' itself only returns the generic Prohibition term and an unrelated song. Left fully unknown -- flag for human review of what this product actually is (category/country not even confirmed).
No web presence found (single product). Own-label blended Scotch pattern, category default applied per the brief's long-tail rule.
Confirmed as one of Tomatin distillery's own blend brands (alongside Antiquary); the infobox marks only the separate Cu Bocan brand as peated, so Talisman/Antiquary/core Tomatin are not peated.
Officially-licensed Irish whiskey blend named after the rock band. No distillery/producer confirmed via citation this session. Category default applied.

Named in a Rest & Be Thankful single-cask sample. Standard, largely blending-only Speyside malt with no known peated identity; peat call is a region-based default, not a Benrinnes-specific citation, hence low confidence.

Named in a Rest & Be Thankful single-cask sample. Wikipedia infobox explicitly labels 'Bruichladdich' (the distillery's own-name releases) as Unpeated, distinct from its siblings Port Charlotte (Heavily Peated) and Octomore (Super-Heavily Peated) -- this row covers only the Bruichladdich-branded unpeated line; Port Charlotte/Octomore are not in this batch's samples so no rows were created for them.
Added as the parent of this batch's 'Talisman' brand. Core Tomatin range is not peated -- only its separate Cu Bocan brand (not in this batch) is flagged peated in the infobox.
